overview.text:
Gujarat runs along a 1,600 km Arabian Sea coast and is the home state of Mahatma Gandhi. Ahmedabad was India's first UNESCO World Heritage City; Gir is the last home of the Asiatic lion; the white Rann of Kutch and Harappan Dholavira lie in the far west.

Pilgrims come for Somnath — first of the twelve Jyotirlingas — and Dwarka, one of the Char Dham.

places.seoTitle: Karnataka Travel Guide: Hampi, Mysuru, Coorg & Coast
places.seoDescription: Plan Karnataka: Bengaluru, Mysuru Palace and Dasara, Coorg, Hampi, Badami and Pattadakal, Gokarna's beaches, Udupi, getting there and the best time to go.

overview.text:
Karnataka packs much of South India into one state. Hampi, capital of the Vijayanagara Empire and a UNESCO site since 1986, has more than 1,600 surviving monuments; further north, Badami was the Chalukya capital, with Pattadakal and Aihole nearby. In the south, Mysuru — the 'Cultural capital of Karnataka' — is famous for its palace and its 10-day Dasara, and the coffee hills of Coorg, the 'Scotland of India', rise in the Western Ghats.

On the coast, Gokarna pairs the Mahabaleshwar Temple with quiet beaches, and Udupi, the 'Temple City', is the home of Udupi cuisine. Bengaluru, the capital, is the usual gateway.

Maddur vada — crisp and fried.
Ragi mudde, the earthy finger-millet ball.
Kundapura koli saaru, a spicy coastal curry.
Holige — a sweet stuffed flatbread.
Shoes off — leave them at the door of temples and mosques; socks are fine.
Right hand — eat, pass and accept things with your right hand.
Dress — cover your legs and shoulders, especially at places of worship.
Photos — don't photograph deities or temple interiors unless it's clearly allowed.

places.name: Maharashtra
places.summary: India's leading state for foreign visitors: Mumbai's heritage and food, the rock-cut caves of Ajanta, Ellora and Elephanta, the Konkan coast and the Western Ghats.
places.seoTitle: Maharashtra Travel Guide: Mumbai, Ajanta, Ellora & Konkan
places.seoDescription: Plan a Maharashtra trip: Mumbai's World Heritage architecture and Elephanta Caves, Ajanta and Ellora, the Konkan coast, Western Ghats treks and local food.

overview.text:
Maharashtra received more foreign tourist visits than any other Indian state in 2024 — 3.70 million — largely because Mumbai, its capital, is one of India's main international gateways. It is the land where Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj founded the Maratha Empire in the 17th century, and its forts and temples still carry that history.

The state's World Heritage Sites span two thousand years: the rock-cut caves of Ajanta, Ellora and Elephanta, and in Mumbai, the Gothic Revival Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus and the Victorian Gothic and Art Deco ensembles around the Oval Maidan. Beyond the cities, the state runs from the beaches of the Konkan coast up into the Sahyadri ranges of the Western Ghats.

Come hungry: vada pav, misal pav, puran poli and modak are all Maharashtrian classics, and Ganesh Chaturthi is celebrated here with more fervour than anywhere else.

items.title: Best time
items.body: December–February, the coolest months

items.title: Capital
items.body: Mumbai (Nagpur is the winter capital)

items.title: Getting in
items.body: Mumbai airport, plus international airports at Pune, Nagpur, Nashik and Shirdi

items.title: Language
items.body: Marathi

items.title: Area
items.body: 307,713 sq km — India's third-largest state

items.title: Monsoon
items.body: Late June to mid-September; wettest in July and August

best_time.text:
Winter (December–February): the coolest months — winter lasts until February, with the lowest temperatures in December and January.

Summer (March–June): temperatures rise steadily from March to June, reaching 40–45 °C on the central plains.

Monsoon (late June–mid-September): the southwest monsoon arrives in the last week of June; July and August are the wettest months.

Post-monsoon (October): the rains fade, though post-monsoon showers still fall now and then.

items.body: Ganesh Chaturthi — the state's biggest festival, between late August and late September, ending with idols immersed in rivers and the sea.
Pandharpur Wari — June–July, when Varkari pilgrims walk to Pandharpur's Vitthal temple for Ashadhi Ekadashi.
Diwali — children build model forts ('killa') in tribute to Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj.
Sawai Gandharva Bhimsen Festival, Pune — one of India's most prestigious Hindustani music festivals.

items.title: Konkan
items.body: The coast between the Western Ghats and the Arabian Sea, a strip 50–80 km wide that includes Mumbai.

items.title: Western Maharashtra (Desh)
items.body: The plateau in the centre of the state, behind the Western Ghats.

items.title: Marathwada
items.body: The Aurangabad Division around Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar — the base for Ajanta and Ellora.

items.title: Vidarbha
items.body: The easternmost region around Nagpur, once part of the Central Provinces and Berar.

items.title: Khandesh
items.body: The north, in the valley of the Tapti and Purna rivers.

how_to_reach.text:
By air: fly into Mumbai (BOM) or Nagpur (NAG); Pune and Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar are the bases for the Western Ghats and the cave sites.

By rail: Mumbai's CSMT and Thane are among India's busiest stations, and the Mumbai Rajdhani is the fastest train from New Delhi.

By road: India's largest road network, with State Transport (ST) buses reaching most towns.

places.name: Punjab
places.summary: Land of the Golden Temple: Amritsar, Sikh heritage at Anandpur Sahib, Patiala's Qila Mubarak, the Harike wetland and famous Punjabi food.
places.seoTitle: Punjab Travel Guide: Amritsar, Golden Temple & More
places.seoDescription: Plan a Punjab trip: Amritsar's Golden Temple and Jallianwala Bagh, Virasat-e-Khalsa at Anandpur Sahib, Patiala's Qila Mubarak and the Harike wetland.

overview.text:
Punjab is the heartland of Sikhism. In Amritsar, the Golden Temple is the faith's spiritual centre, where the langar serves free meals to all, and nearby Jallianwala Bagh recalls the massacre of 1919. At Anandpur Sahib, Virasat-e-Khalsa tells the story of the Sikh community, and the town hosts Hola Mohalla, a festival of martial arts and culture.

Beyond the Sikh sites, Patiala's Qila Mubarak and Kapurthala's mirrored Sheesh Mahal, inspired by Versailles, recall the state's royal past, and Harike Wetland, where the Beas and Sutlej meet, is the largest wetland in northern India. Punjab recorded 27.7 million domestic and 0.54 million foreign tourist visits in 2024.

items.title: Winter
items.body: December–February: frosty, with nights below 5 °C

items.title: Capital
items.body: Chandigarh (shared with Haryana)

items.title: Getting in
items.body: Amritsar airport, or Chandigarh (Mohali)

items.title: Language
items.body: Punjabi (Gurmukhi script)

items.title: Summer
items.body: Mid-April–June; Ludhiana tops 41 °C

items.title: Area
items.body: 50,362 sq km

best_time.text:
Spring (March–mid-April): the mild change from winter to summer.

Summer (mid-April–June): hot — Ludhiana stays above 41 °C for about six weeks.

Monsoon (early July–September): the rainy season.

Autumn (September–November): the post-monsoon change towards winter.

Winter (December–February): cold, with ground frost and nights below 5 °C for almost two months.

items.title: Majha
items.body: Between the Ravi and Beas rivers — the Amritsar side of the state.

items.title: Doaba
items.body: Between the Sutlej and Beas rivers.

items.title: Malwa
items.body: South of the Sutlej — the largest region.

items.title: Puadh
items.body: Near the Ghaggar river, by Chandigarh.
Lohri — bonfires and folk dance, usually 13 January.
Hola Mohalla, Anandpur Sahib — three days of Sikh martial displays, usually March.
Baisakhi — the harvest festival, 13 or 14 April.
Diwali — celebrated with great pomp.
Gurdwaras — cover your head; caps or cloths are usually lent free.
Langar — gurdwaras serve free community meals; join in.
Shoes off — leave them at the door of temples and mosques; socks are fine.
Right hand — eat, pass and accept things with your right hand.

how_to_reach.text:
By air: Amritsar's Sri Guru Ram Das Ji International Airport is the main gateway, with direct flights to London, Birmingham, Milan, Dubai and Singapore; Chandigarh (Mohali) is also international.

By rail: Vande Bharat and Shatabdi trains link New Delhi with Amritsar, 449 km away; other main stations are Ludhiana, Jalandhar, Pathankot and Patiala.

places.name: Tamil Nadu
places.summary: Temple country of the south: Pallava and Chola monuments, Chennai, the Nilgiri hills and Tamil food, music and dance.
places.seoTitle: Tamil Nadu Travel Guide: Chennai, Temples & Mahabalipuram
places.seoDescription: Plan a Tamil Nadu trip: Chennai, the Pallava monuments of Mahabalipuram, the Great Living Chola Temples, the Nilgiri Mountain Railway, food and festivals.

overview.text:
Tamil Nadu recorded 306.8 million domestic tourist visits in 2024 — the second most of any state — and 1.16 million foreign visits. It is above all a land of temples: its World Heritage Sites include the Pallava monuments of Mahabalipuram and the Great Living Chola Temples, alongside the Nilgiri Mountain Railway.

Tamil culture is a draw in its own right — Carnatic music, Bharatanatyam dance, and meals served on a banana leaf with sambar and coconut chutney. Pongal, the harvest festival, is the year's great celebration.

Most visitors start in Chennai, the capital, and follow the coast south to Mahabalipuram and on to Puducherry.

places.name: West Bengal
places.summary: From Kolkata's culture and Durga Puja to the Sundarbans mangroves and the tea hills of Darjeeling.
places.seoTitle: West Bengal Travel Guide: Kolkata, Darjeeling & Sundarbans
places.seoDescription: Plan a West Bengal trip: Kolkata's museums and Durga Puja, the Sundarbans, Bishnupur's terracotta temples, Darjeeling's toy train and Bengali sweets.

overview.text:
West Bengal runs from the Bay of Bengal to the Himalaya. Kolkata, its capital, is known as India's cultural capital and is home to the Indian Museum, founded in 1814, and the Victoria Memorial; Bishnupur has terracotta temples, and the Sundarbans mangrove forest is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. In the north lie the tea gardens of Darjeeling.

The state's grandest festival is Durga Puja, celebrated over nine days with elaborate pandals, and Bengali food — from hilsa to rasogolla and sandesh — is a highlight of any trip. West Bengal received 3.12 million foreign tourist visits in 2024, second among Indian states.

items.title: Winter
items.body: December–January: mild on the plains (about 15 °C at night)

items.title: Capital
items.body: Kolkata

items.title: Getting in
items.body: Kolkata airport; Bagdogra (near Siliguri) for the hills

items.title: Languages
items.body: Bengali and English; Nepali in the Darjeeling hills

items.title: Monsoon
items.body: June–September

items.title: Area
items.body: 88,752 sq km

best_time.text:
Winter (December–January): mild on the plains, with nights around 15 °C; the Darjeeling hills have a harsh winter with occasional snow.

Summer (before the rains): very humid in the delta, with sudden nor'wester storms (Kalbaisakhi) early in the season.

Monsoon (June–September): rain across the state; Darjeeling, Jalpaiguri and Cooch Behar get more than 250 cm.

Autumn (short, around Durga Puja): a brief season between the rains and winter, when Durga Puja fills the state in Ashvin (September–October).

items.body: Durga Puja — September–October, with pandals across the state; UNESCO-listed.
Kali Puja — celebrated at Diwali.
Lakshmi Puja — honouring the goddess of wealth.
Poush Mela, Santiniketan — the annual harvest fair.

how_to_reach.text:
By air: Kolkata's Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose International is the main airport; Bagdogra, near Siliguri, is the gateway to Darjeeling and the hills, with flights to Bhutan and Thailand; Andal serves Asansol and Durgapur.

By rail: about 4,481 km of railway links the state.

By road: state buses — Calcutta, North Bengal and South Bengal State Transport — run across West Bengal.
